name: e01 starter model and constant-share reference
expectation:
Starter: top choice matched about 29% (build) and 28% (check), as run_baseline.py prints.
I expect its log loss to be WORSE than the constant-share reference, because its weights are
hand-set and it underpredicts the entrant (15.9% vs 21.1%). Constant reference log loss should
be near the entropy of the shares, about 1.59 on build.

outputs.note: The starter is not trained on any data, so scoring it on check uses up nothing.

verdict: WRONG expectation: starter log loss 1.579 beats the constant reference 1.594 on build (and 1.563 vs 1.591 on check). But only by about 1%, so the hand-set weights carry very little signal. Bar for any new model: clearly below 1.58.

name: e02 household bootstrap of lever gaps
expectation:
Price: $3.49 minus $5.49 entrant share interval excludes zero, roughly +10 to +22 points.
Message: environment minus low_odor is borderline; I expect the lower end of the interval near 0.
Cleaning vs the others: interval includes zero.
Channel: online minus retail is borderline, lower end near or below 0.
Household resampling gives wider intervals than visit resampling, by 10-30%.
verdict: MIXED. Price confirmed: 3.49 vs 5.49 = +16.1 pts [11.2, 21.1]. Clustering concern WRONG for gaps: household and visit intervals are the same width (ratio 0.91-1.03), because each household saw several levels, so its own taste cancels in a gap. Households do differ (entrant-count variance 1.58 vs 1.00 binomial), so clustering still matters for levels. By my FIRST.md rule, environment vs low_odor [1.8, 13.4] and online vs retail [0.8, 9.5] pass. But I picked environment vs low_odor because it was the largest raw gap, and 7 gaps were tested; both lower ends are close to 0. I do NOT yet treat message or channel as settled. Next: a stricter test declared in advance.

name: e03 grow the learned model one idea at a time
expectation:
(I already fit model A once while testing the code: train log loss 1.58, price weight -0.46.)
A: cross-validated log loss about 1.585, no better than the starter (1.579).
B: usual brand helps clearly, CV log loss about 1.55, usual-brand weight about +0.5.
B+msg and B+chan: each improves CV log loss by less than 0.003, maybe none.

RULE, decided now: I call message or channel "real" only if BOTH
  (1) its Wald test inside model C has p < 0.01 (strict, because I test several things), and
  (2) adding it to B lowers cross-validated log loss.
My guess: message p between 0.01 and 0.1 and channel p about 0.03, so both FAIL the rule.
verdict: MOSTLY CONFIRMED, one surprise. A = 1.587 as guessed. Usual brand weight +0.49 as guessed, but B only reaches 1.575, not the 1.55 I expected: knowing the household helps much less than I thought. Message p=0.057 and channel p=0.026, both fail the pre-declared rule (p<0.01 AND lower CV loss); CV gains are tiny (0.0009 and 0.0004). Big lesson: every model sits near 1.575-1.59, so most of each choice is not predictable from these fields. Tight budget makes price matter a bit more (-0.083 +/- 0.043), not clear.

name: e04 does history help
expectation:
Stage 1 showed households repeat their last choice only 23.1% vs 20.6% by chance, so:
same_as_last_visit small and positive (about +0.15), not clear (p > 0.05).
none_after_buying_last_visit near zero (the starter assumes it is positive; I doubt it).
entrant_bought_before positive; entrant_bad_note_before negative.
Overall D improves CV log loss over C (1.5741) by less than 0.005.
RULE: history is worth carrying between visits only if D beats C in CV log loss.
verdict: PARTLY WRONG. History helps a little: CV 1.5741 -> 1.5701, rule passes. But the gain comes from ONE thing: entrant_bought_before +0.56 (z=3.4). same_as_last_visit is 0.00, not +0.15 as I guessed. none_after_buying is ~0 (z=0.5), so the starter's built-in idea is not supported. Bad entrant note -0.82 (z=-1.9) on only 51 visits: a hint, not proof. CAVEAT: 'bought before' may just mean some households liked the entrant from the start; this data cannot tell taste from 'trying it made them like it'. What the model carries between visits: did they buy the entrant before, and what note they gave it.
